critical_code_review_comments: PUBLIC_PREFIXES list in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js is a single source of truth for 'this route needs no session' — it's out of sync with the actual public routes declared in App.js (/p/:slug, /share/:token). Extract PUBLIC_PATHS/PUBLIC_PREFIXES from Router config or add a lint rule so new public routes must be registered in both places. Otherwise this bug will re-appear each time.

routes/dev_publish.py deploy_vercel/deploy_netlify: user access token is passed straight to httpx and NEVER logged, good. But on transient httpx.HTTPError (network flake / DNS), it will bubble out as an unhandled 500. Wrap the httpx.AsyncClient block in try/except httpx.HTTPError → HTTPException(502, 'Vercel unreachable') to preserve the clean-error contract we tested for.

routes/dev_publish.py _serve_prod injects /routes/dev_os.py _inject_login_shim into html; that import is inside the function (lazy). If dev_os.py errors at import time in some future refactor, prod pages 500. Consider moving _inject_login_shim to a shared util module.

services/dev_chat_agents.py _llm_build_ideas — 500-char brief truncation is fine for OpenAI but not enforced on the 4-chip response, so a chatty gpt-4o-mini could return 4 chips whose combined JSON blows past the model's ~1k output budget and falls through to _FALLBACK_IDEAS. Consider system-prompting a max prompt length of ~120 chars.

rca of the issue.reproduction: 1) Open incognito tab (no tn_session cookie). 2) Navigate directly to https://nest-app-prep.preview.emergentagent.com/p/engineering-project. 3) Observe URL immediately becomes / and the WebHome marketing page renders instead of ProductionAppPage.
rca of the issue.root_cause: AuthProvider (in AuthContext.jsx) fires GET /api/auth/me on every SPA load to detect an existing session. Without a cookie it returns 401. The global axios response interceptor at /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js line 49-59 catches every 401 and, if the current pathname is NOT in PUBLIC_PATHS or covered by PUBLIC_PREFIXES, executes `window.location.href = '/'`. PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ['/join/', '/s/'] — it does NOT include '/p/'. So even though App.js registers <Route path='/p/:slug' element={<ProductionAppPage />}/> as a truly public route outside the AppShell auth guard, the axios interceptor evicts the visitor to '/' before ProductionAppPage ever fetches /api/p/{slug}/index.html.
rca of the issue.mitigation: One-line change in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js: `const PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ['/join/', '/s/', '/p/', '/share/'];`. Also add a comment tying this list to the routes defined in App.js so drift is caught in code review. Longer-term: expose a single PUBLIC_ROUTES module consumed by both App.js and api.js so the two lists cannot diverge.
